questions.explain: The chapter says authentication mode is the first thing to check when a login fails that should work — a SQL login cannot authenticate against a Windows-only instance, and the error log won't always make that obvious.
options: The password policy was enforced
Mixed Mode was enabled
The SQL login has a weak password
The instance is in Windows-only authentication mode, so a SQL login cannot authenticate at all
questions.q: A SQL Server login fails to authenticate even though the credentials are correct. What is the first configuration the chapter says to check?

questions.explain: The chapter recommends disabling and renaming sa in most production environments, so attackers cannot target a known account name; for break-glass, use a long random password in a vault and alert on any use.
options: Enable it for all application connections
Disable and rename it, and alert on any break-glass use
Delete the login entirely from sys.server_principals
Give it the db_datareader role on all databases
questions.q: What does the chapter recommend for the sa login in production?

questions.explain: In SQL Server RLS, filter predicates are enforced on reads; db_owner members bypass RLS predicates by default, so service/ETL accounts must be designed with that in mind.
options: Members of db_owner bypass RLS predicates by default
The sa login is the only bypass
Nobody can bypass a SECURITY POLICY
RCSI must be enabled first
questions.q: In SQL Server Row-Level Security, which principals bypass the policy predicates by default?

questions.explain: The chapter explains the certificate protects the TDE database encryption key; without it your backups are unrecoverable — so back it up immediately and store it off-server.
options: It is needed to read the audit logs
It is required before you can enable RCSI
The certificate and private key must be backed up immediately and stored off-server, because without them your backups are unrecoverable
It allows the database to be restored on any instance automatically
questions.q: Why must you back up the TDE certificate and private key immediately after enabling Transparent Data Encryption?

questions.explain: The chapter says predicate columns must be indexed (e.g., a composite index on tenant_id, created_at) because every query against the protected table gets the predicate joined in, and unindexed predicate columns cause full table scans.
options: Index the columns referenced in the RLS predicates, or every query risks a full table scan
Set the recovery model to SIMPLE
Disable auto-update statistics on the protected table
Create the predicate function without SCHEMABINDING
questions.q: What performance requirement does the chapter place on Row-Level Security predicate columns?
